info.title: Jarvis Operator API
info.summary: A safety-gated API for the Jarvis Z-State runtime and durable operator data.
info.description: Jarvis accepts structured operator requests, routes work through its runtime and safety envelope, persists tasks and reminders through the configured JSON or Convex provider, runs proposal-only Totality reasoning, stages revision-checked project-memory changes, and stores revision-bound tool-action proposals for explicit approval or rejection without execution. The private development ChatGPT App preview now provides a stateless Streamable HTTP MCP adapter and versioned dashboard widget for the operations marked with x-mcp-tool.exposed=true. Jarvis and OpenAI credentials remain server-side. This contract is intentionally single-user and private.

x-jarvis-architecture.businessBoundary: Jarvis routes business-domain work through integrations and must not duplicate authoritative TBTB business logic.

x-chatgpt-app.credentialHandling: The MCP server injects JARVIS_SERVICE_TOKEN server-side. The model, widget, and tool arguments never receive it.
x-chatgpt-app.remoteExposureRequirement: Require OAuth 2.1 at the MCP boundary before any remote or multi-user deployment.

get.description: Returns process liveness without touching persistence or exposing configuration.
Returns the stable operator-facing capability map for the subset of this contract implemented by the running adapter.

get.summary: Inspect Jarvis runtime and provider status
get.description: Checks storage reachability, authentication, schema compatibility, layer readiness, timezone, and Z-State activation without returning secrets.

x-mcp-tool.title: Check Jarvis status
x-mcp-tool.description: Use this when the user asks whether Jarvis, its storage provider, safety gates, or Z-State layers are healthy and ready.

post.description: Parses one text input, constructs an execution plan, routes each step, evaluates the complete output through the immutable safety envelope, and returns the result. ChatGPT should use focused task and reminder tools instead of exposing this broad runtime endpoint as an MCP tool.

200.description: The conversation turn completed and passed the safety gate.

get.description: Returns the authoritative task list from the configured persistence provider.

x-mcp-tool.title: List Jarvis tasks
x-mcp-tool.description: Use this when the user wants to see, review, summarise, or choose from their current Jarvis tasks.

post.description: Creates one task after explicit user intent. Reusing an Idempotency-Key must replay the original result rather than create a duplicate.

x-mcp-tool.title: Create a Jarvis task
x-mcp-tool.description: Use this when the user explicitly asks Jarvis to save one new task with a title and category.

Location.description: Canonical URL of the created task.

get.description: Returns one task by its opaque provider-issued identifier.

x-mcp-tool.title: Get a Jarvis task
x-mcp-tool.description: Use this when the user refers to one known Jarvis task identifier and its current authoritative fields are needed.

patch.description: Updates the supplied task title and/or category without changing identity, completion, or creation time.

x-mcp-tool.title: Update a Jarvis task
x-mcp-tool.description: Use this when the user explicitly asks to change the title or category of one existing Jarvis task.

delete.description: Permanently removes one task after explicit user confirmation.

x-mcp-tool.title: Delete a Jarvis task
x-mcp-tool.description: Use this only when the user explicitly asks to permanently remove one identified Jarvis task.

200.description: Task deleted. The removed record is returned for confirmation.

post.description: Sets the task completed flag to true. Repeated calls leave the task completed.

x-mcp-tool.title: Complete a Jarvis task
x-mcp-tool.description: Use this when the user explicitly says one identified Jarvis task is complete or done.

get.description: Returns the authoritative reminder list from the configured persistence provider.

x-mcp-tool.title: List Jarvis reminders
x-mcp-tool.description: Use this when the user wants to see, review, summarise, or choose from their current Jarvis reminders.

post.description: Creates one reminder and preserves its exact due text. Jarvis only adds a timestamp when the due value is unambiguous in the supplied timezone.

x-mcp-tool.title: Create a Jarvis reminder
x-mcp-tool.description: Use this when the user explicitly asks Jarvis to save one reminder with a title and optional due text.

Location.description: Canonical URL of the created reminder.

get.description: Returns one reminder by its opaque provider-issued identifier.

x-mcp-tool.title: Get a Jarvis reminder
x-mcp-tool.description: Use this when the user refers to one known Jarvis reminder identifier and its current authoritative fields are needed.

patch.description: Updates the supplied title and/or due value. Sending due=null explicitly clears all due fields.

x-mcp-tool.title: Update a Jarvis reminder
x-mcp-tool.description: Use this when the user explicitly asks to change the title or due value of one existing Jarvis reminder.

delete.description: Permanently removes one reminder after explicit user confirmation.

x-mcp-tool.title: Delete a Jarvis reminder
x-mcp-tool.description: Use this only when the user explicitly asks to permanently remove one identified Jarvis reminder.

200.description: Reminder deleted. The removed record is returned for confirmation.

get.description: Takes one coherent persistence snapshot and returns a version 2 Jarvis backup archive. This sensitive operation is intentionally excluded from the model tool surface.

post.description: Validates a version 1 or 2 archive and verifies it in isolated storage without touching the configured live provider.

post.summary: Restore a backup into an empty provider
post.description: Restores a verified archive only when the configured target has no assistant state, tasks, or reminders. The confirmation field must be exactly true. This operation is never exposed as a model tool.

200.description: Archive restored and returned references remapped.

post.summary: Run proposal-only Totality reasoning with validation and audit journalling
post.description: Runs proposal-only Totality reasoning against bounded authoritative project context. Successful typed memory suggestions are validated locally and staged as approval-required project-memory change sets in the same Convex transaction as validation and audit evidence. No memory is approved or applied by this operation.

200.description: The reasoning draft was validated and journalled.

422.description: The request or authority policy is invalid.

get.description: Lists bounded, owner-scoped memory change sets, optionally filtered by state.

post.summary: Stage typed project-memory changes for explicit approval
post.description: Stages one idempotent change set against the current project revision without writing canonical memory.

get.description: Returns one staged memory change set without modifying its state.

post.summary: Approve a revision-matched project-memory change set
post.description: Transitions the memory change set to approved without writing canonical memory.

post.summary: Reject a staged project-memory change set
post.description: Transitions the memory change set to rejected without writing canonical memory.

post.summary: Transactionally apply an approved project-memory change set
post.description: Applies all approved records, increments the project revision, and appends audit evidence in one Convex transaction.

get.description: Returns recent tool-action proposals for one project. This operation cannot execute a tool.

post.summary: Stage a tool-action proposal for explicit review
post.description: Stores one idempotent proposal against the authoritative project revision. Staging never calls the named tool.

get.description: Returns one proposal and its approval state without invoking the named tool.

post.description: Records explicit operator approval after checking the project revision. Approval does not execute the proposal.
Records an explicit rejection reason. Rejection does not call the named tool.

Runs an approved proposal against the tool/operation allowlist and returns a durable receipt. Blocked, timed-out, and failed outcomes are returned as a receipt with a 200 status, not as an error, since the attempt itself always completes. Currently no tool/operation is allowlisted, so every call returns a receipt with status "blocked" and errorCode "not-allowlisted" until a specific definition is registered server-side.

200.description: Execution attempt completed (successfully, blocked, timed out, or failed) and recorded as a durable receipt.

get.description: Returns the authoritative client list from the configured client store.

post.description: Creates one client after explicit user intent.

get.description: Returns one client by its opaque identifier.

patch.description: Updates the name, contacts, or notes of one client.

delete.description: Permanently removes one client by its identifier.

get.description: Returns the authoritative project list.

post.description: Creates one project linked to a client.

get.description: Returns one project by identifier.

patch.description: Updates client, title, status, or notes.

get.description: Returns the authoritative list of quote aggregate/revision snapshots. Requires the Convex persistence provider.

post.summary: Create a quote and its first revision
post.description: Creates one quote aggregate and its draft revision 1; totals are derived server-side from the line items. Requires the Convex persistence provider.

get.description: Returns the current aggregate and current revision for one quote. Requires the Convex persistence provider.

patch.description: Applies a partial patch to a draft revision after checking the expected aggregate and revision versions. Requires the Convex persistence provider.

post.summary: Submit a draft revision for review
post.description: Transitions a draft revision to reviewed after checking the expected aggregate and revision versions. Requires the Convex persistence provider.

post.summary: Reopen a reviewed revision for editing
post.description: Transitions a reviewed revision back to draft after checking the expected aggregate and revision versions. Requires the Convex persistence provider.

Transitions a reviewed revision to finalized and computes its immutable fingerprint, after checking the expected aggregate and revision versions. Finalized revisions cannot be edited further. Requires the Convex persistence provider.

post.summary: Fork a new draft revision from a finalized revision
post.description: Creates the next numbered draft revision from an exact-fingerprint-matched finalized revision, after checking the expected aggregate and revision versions. Requires the Convex persistence provider.

201.description: New draft revision created from the finalized revision.

post.description: Records the accepted, declined, or expired outcome against the exact finalized revision, after checking the expected aggregate version. Requires the Convex persistence provider.

get.description: Returns delivery attempts for one quote's revisions, newest first. 503 outside the configured Convex persistence provider.
Composes a read-only digest of open tasks, due reminders, active projects, and outstanding quotes. Derived on request from the authoritative stores; nothing is stored.
Returns the authoritative errand list, including any stored locations.

post.description: Creates one pick-up-on-the-way item, optionally tagged with a structured location resolved at the conversation layer. The server stores locations; it never geocodes.

get.description: Returns one errand by identifier.

patch.description: Updates fields; marking an errand done stamps its completion time once, and reopening clears it.

get.description: Returns the authoritative list of Benny's builds and machines.

post.description: Records one machine or project — the RC crawler, the trailer, a tool.

get.description: Returns one build by identifier.

patch.description: Updates a build's name, kind, status, description, nickname, or notes.

get.description: Returns the authoritative, owner+project-scoped list of durable notes. Note creation is not exposed here: it stays on the governed tool-actions execute path (POST /api/v1/projects/{projectId}/tool-actions), which is where the mandatory idempotency/fingerprint contract on note creation is actually enforced.
Returns one owner+project-scoped note by identifier.

delete.description: Deletes one owner+project-scoped note by identifier.

get.description: Returns the dated lore attached to Benny's builds — origins, milestones, failures, anecdotes, notes.

post.description: Adds one dated entry to a build's story — why it started, a milestone, a failure, an anecdote, or a loose note.

get.description: Returns one build log entry by identifier.

patch.description: Updates a build log entry's build, kind, title, body, or occurred time.

delete.description: Permanently removes one build log entry.

get.description: Returns the upgrade chronicle — the changes made to Benny's builds over time.

post.description: Records one change to a build — what was swapped or modified, why, the before/after, the outcome, and the parts involved.

get.description: Returns one upgrade by identifier.

patch.description: Updates an upgrade's build, title, reason, before/after state, outcome, parts, version, or occurred time.

get.description: Returns Benny's tools and machines with derived maintenance status (next due, overdue).

post.description: Records one tool or machine to keep on top of servicing, with an optional service interval and last-serviced date.

get.description: Returns one asset by identifier with derived maintenance status.

patch.description: Updates an asset's name, kind, service interval, last-serviced date, or notes.

get.description: Returns Benny's settings and standing choices — brands, tools, naming, defaults.

post.description: Records one standing choice as a key/value pair, with an optional category.

get.description: Returns one preference by identifier.

patch.description: Updates a preference's key, value, or category.

serviceToken.description: Single-user Jarvis service token. Send it only in the Authorization header. Never place it in URLs, logs, tool arguments, widget state, or model-visible output.

BadRequest.description: The request could not be parsed or violated the transport contract.

Unauthorized.description: The service token is missing, invalid, or revoked.

NotFound.description: The requested record does not exist for this owner.

Conflict.description: The request conflicts with current state, an idempotency key, or an empty-target requirement.

PayloadTooLarge.description: The backup archive exceeds the 10 MiB limit.

UnprocessableEntity.description: The request is syntactically valid but violates Jarvis validation or safety rules.

TooManyRequests.description: The caller has exceeded the configured request rate.

Retry-After.description: Seconds before the caller should retry.

ServiceUnavailable.description: A required persistence, reliability, or safety dependency is unavailable.

InternalServerError.description: Jarvis failed without exposing credentials or internal exception details.

RecordId.description: Opaque identifier. Clients must not parse provider-specific structure.

sourceVersion.description: Build commit or immutable source identifier.

context.description: Small task-specific context only. Do not send full conversation transcripts or credentials.

text.description: Exact due text to preserve, such as tomorrow 9am or after Claire calls.

timezone.description: IANA timezone used only for local wall-clock input. Defaults to the configured Jarvis timezone.

AssistantState.description: JSON-safe Jarvis runtime state. It may contain provider record references that are remapped during restore.

BackupArchiveInput.description: A version 1 or version 2 Jarvis backup archive. Version 1 is accepted for migration compatibility.

confirmEmptyTarget.description: Explicit acknowledgement that restore is permitted only into an empty provider.

taskIds.description: Map from archive task IDs to restored provider IDs.

reminderIds.description: Map from archive reminder IDs to restored provider IDs.

detail.description: Safe operator-facing detail with credentials and internal exception data removed.

approvalToken.description: A separately configured operator secret, distinct from the Bearer service token, that proves a human decided to approve this specific proposal.

arguments.description: Bounded JSON arguments. Credential-bearing keys, secrets, non-finite numbers, excessive nesting, and oversized strings are rejected before persistence.

idempotencyKey.description: Owner-scoped replay key that cannot be rebound to another action ID.

arguments.description: Bounded JSON arguments. Credential-bearing keys, secrets, non-finite numbers, excessive nesting, and oversized strings are rejected before persistence.

destructive.description: When true, requiredAuthority must be T3. This still does not authorise execution.

idempotencyKey.description: Owner-scoped replay key that cannot be rebound to another action ID.
Replay key for this specific execution attempt. The same key against the same action returns the identical receipt rather than executing again.

dryRun.description: When true, validates authority/allowlist/arguments and returns a receipt without calling the tool.

timeoutMs.description: Bounds how long the executed operation may run before it is aborted as timed out. Defaults to 5000ms.

outputDigest.description: SHA-256 digest of the tool's output. The output itself is never persisted or returned.

due.description: Read-only. Derived: true when nextDueAt is known and has passed.
